source_name: DAE, Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 2783, answered 17.12.2025
source_location: Answer (b), PDF page 1: 'The Government has drawn up a roadmap to reach a capacity of 100 GW by 2047, of which NPCIL will contributing 54 GW by 2047 by setting up new nuclear power plants based on indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors and Light Water Reactors with foreign cooperation.'
notes: Low case: NPCIL's part of the mission only, so a lower bound on utility nuclear in 2047 (other PSUs and private companies left out). No captive units: the captive reactors of answers (c) and (d) (BSMR-200, SMR-55 and the Bharat Small Reactors offered to industries as captive plants) are not NPCIL's 54 GW of PHWR and LWR plants. CUF 0.68: the CEA NEP 2022-32 nuclear availability (Annexure 5.1, printed page 5.28, PDF page 154), the CUF of the nuclear rows of build_limits.csv. Energy = 54,000 MW / 1000 x 0.68 x 8.76 = 321.7 TWh, our computation. Capacity-based by design: the CUF turns the published MW into energy, and installed capacity is never forecast. Secondary source.

source_name: CEA, Road Map for Achieving the Goal of 100 GW of Nuclear Capacity by 2047 (committee report constituted by MoP OM of 27.02.2025; signed 27.06.2025; released 11.10.2025, PIB Release ID 2177769)
source_location: Table 6.3 'Technology wise expected installed capacity in 2047', printed page 25 (PDF page 50): cumulative till 2047 1,00,648 MW, of which BSR 5,060 MW and BSMR 5,000 MW
notes: Captive units left out by the organisers' ruling (captive generation is outside NPP utility generation): BSR 5,060 MW + BSMR 5,000 MW = 10,060 MW (Table 5.3 note, printed page 16, PDF page 41: 'Includes BSR/BSMR/SMR for captive uses'; DAE Lok Sabha USQ 2783, 17.12.2025, answers (c) and (d): BSMR-200 and SMR-55 'can be deployed as captive plant', and Bharat Small Reactors offered to industries 'as captive plants'). Utility capacity 90,588 MW. CUF 0.68 as in the low case. Energy = 90,588 MW / 1000 x 0.68 x 8.76 = 539.6 TWh, our computation. The mission itself: Union Budget 2025-26, Budget Speech Part A, paragraphs 61-62, printed page 11 (PDF page 15), https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/budget_speech.pdf: 'Development of at least 100 GW of nuclear energy by 2047 is essential for our energy transition efforts.' The CEA URL https://cea.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/notification/2025/10/Roadmap_Final_30062025.pdf returned 404 on 2026-11-22; the archived copy in source_url was read. Secondary source.

source_name: CEA, Road Map for Achieving the Goal of 100 GW of Nuclear Capacity by 2047 (committee report constituted by MoP OM of 27.02.2025; signed 27.06.2025; released 11.10.2025, PIB Release ID 2177769)
source_location: Table 6.3, printed page 25 (PDF page 50), as in the central case; PLF: paragraph 11.1.3.1 (c) 'Enhancing Normative PLF to 80% from present norm of 72.5%', printed page 52 (PDF page 77): 'it should be possible to achieve PLF of 80% in new PHWR units'; 'The normative PLF for PWR is already 80%.'
notes: High case: the central utility fleet (90,588 MW, captive units left out as in the central case) at the road map's achievable PLF. The same paragraph gives an actual fleet PLF of 'about 79%' in 2024-25. Energy = 90,588 MW / 1000 x 0.80 x 8.76 = 634.8 TWh, our computation. The nuclear build cap credits each published GW at the CUF of build_limits.csv (0.68), so this case can lie above the cap; the model then reports the plan as infeasible rather than cut the floor. Secondary source.
